To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured the Ks, Lambda, and Xi spectra at the STAR detector in Au+Au collisions.

We measured the Ks, Lambda, Xi- and Anti-Lambda yields in the most central Au+Au collisions for \sqrt{s_Nn} = 7-39 GeV and found that the ratios of Lambda, Xi- over pions and Anti-Lambda over pions are well described by statistical hadronization models at all three energies.

The K0s, Lambda, Xi and Omega yields are consistent with the predictions from statistical hadronization models, indicating the dominance of hadronic freeze-out processes in the hadronization of the system created in Au+Au collisions from 7.7 to 39 GeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the hadron production and the hadronization mechanism in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
the study of the production and properties of light nuclei and hypernuclei in relativistic heavy ion collisions.
the production of Ks, Xi- and pion ratios from Au+Au and Pb+Pb collision data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the measured particle ratios are consistent with a hadronization process in which a thermalized system of quarks and gluons (QGP) is produced in the collisions.
the measured particle ratios at all three energies are consistent with the predictions from statistical hadronization.
these ratios are not very sensitive to the collision energy and the system size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the statistical hadronization is applicable to the most central collisions at SPS, RHIC, and now also LHC, for the first time.
the hadronization mechanism is the same at RHIC and SPS, and that the chemical freeze-out temperature and the baryo-chemical potential are energy independent.
the hadronization mechanism is independent of the beam energy from SPS to RHIC energies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the measured yields of Ks, Xi and Lambda at 7.7 and 11.5 GeV are comparable to those measured at SPS energies and that the yields of Xi and Lambda are similar at all three energies.
the hadronic freezeout temperature is energy independent in the SPS energy regime.
the hadronization mechanism in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC-NSD energies is consistent with a hadronization mechanism seen at the SPS.
